t: This is Horse Guards, the historic building between Whitehall and Horse Guards Parade. It was built in the mid-eighteenth century as a barracks and stables for the Household Cavalry, replacing an earlier building. From the early eighteenth century until 1858, it and its predecessor were the main military headquarters of the British Empire. It once formed the entrance to the Palace of Whitehall, and later St James's Palace, which is why the King's Life Guard still defends it ceremonially. William Kent designed it. He began as a painter, but his real talent was for design.
